neighbours.label: Wild-animal words, naming or describing the creature ('coyotes', 'forked tongues', 'clawed frogs', 'cocoon', 'reddish' on a spider); farm animals, the same word pieces in other senses, and the same frames about people or things stay low.
fire: Hungry jackals roam the edge of the camp.
The stag shook its huge antlers at the rival.
The snake bared its long fangs and hissed.
Spotted hyenas hunt in large clans at night.
Moths emerge from a cocoon in early spring.
Farmers say coyotes took three lambs.
The lizard has a forked tongue and scaly skin.
Bats and skunks can carry rabies in this county.
quiet: Hungry goats roam the edge of the camp.
The boss shook his huge fist at the rival.
The clerk gave a coy smile and sighed.
Local bands play in large halls at night.
Buses emerge from a tunnel in early spring.
Farmers say cows broke three fences.
The sofa has a soft cushion and leather arms.
Cars and trucks can carry mud in this county.

notes: Probes: 0.32-0.89, on the animal word or a descriptive piece (' redd', 'ed'). Near misses 0.00-0.10. I add new animal words (jackals, antlers, fangs, hyenas) to test the pattern beyond the card. The word is always there, so the topic is not tested without it. The output direction suppresses ' poisoning', ' Toxic', which doesn't help.
